investment_summary:
Broadcom's FY2025 (ended November 2, 2025) revenue rose 24% to $63,887 million, and operating income nearly doubled to $25,484 million, with gross margin back at 68% [1]. AI networking and custom accelerators drove semiconductors, while VMware Cloud Foundation drove infrastructure software, where operating income rose 49% to $20,765 million [1].

Consensus dated after the 10-K expects FY2026 revenue of $105,981 million (+65.9%) and EPS of $11.65, at 24.6x forward earnings, and the last four quarters all beat EPS estimates [3].

Valuation is the key question. At an enterprise value of about $1.47 trillion, the reverse DCF requires 26.6% annual revenue growth for ten years. That is close to the 24.4% three-year historical CAGR but far below consensus growth of roughly 65% for FY2026 and FY2027 [2][3]. The 19.3% implied return assumes the consensus path is delivered. Net debt fell to $48,958 million, but customer concentration and gross margin pressure from AI racks remain the main risks [1].
key_takeaways: AI-driven margin expansion should persist as software mix holds: operating margin reached 40% against 26% a year earlier [1].
Consensus growth of about 65% in FY2026 is demanding against a 24% historical pace, so upside depends on AI delivery [2][3].
Net debt fell to $48,958 million and free cash flow reached $26,914 million, so funding looks secure in the near term [1][2].
Customer concentration and the gross margin cost of AI racks are the main risks to a premium multiple [1][3].
business_overview:
Broadcom Inc. designs and supplies semiconductor solutions and infrastructure software, with roots going back more than 60 years to AT&T/Bell Labs, Lucent and Hewlett-Packard. In fiscal 2025, which ended November 2, 2025, net revenue rose 24% to $63,887 million from $51,574 million. Semiconductor solutions contributed $36,858 million (58%) and infrastructure software $27,029 million (42%) [1]. Segment operating income rose 27% to $21,232 million in semiconductors and 49% to $20,765 million in software [1]. The company holds about 19,000 patents, and 57% of its roughly 33,000 employees work in research and development [1].

The semiconductor franchise includes custom AI accelerators (XPUs), Ethernet switching and routing, NICs and optical components, alongside FBAR-based RF filters, PCIe and storage controllers, and set-top box and broadband SoCs [1]. The software portfolio centres on VMware Cloud Foundation, mainframe tools, and Symantec and Carbon Black security products [1]. The filing describes software revenue as relying on multi-year enterprise license agreements, which makes it a steadier stream than semiconductors [1]. Most manufacturing is outsourced, with TSMC as the main foundry, while internal fabs serve proprietary processes [1].

Strategy has centred on the VMware acquisition, which closed on November 22, 2023. Since then Broadcom sold the End-User Computing business to KKR for $3.5 billion (July 1, 2024), bought Seagate's SoC operations for $600 million (April 23, 2024), and moved VMware products to subscription licensing with VCF license portability [1]. In fiscal 2025 it paid $11,142 million in dividends and repurchased $2,450 million of stock [1]. Capital expenditure was $623 million and is expected to rise in fiscal 2026 [1]. Analyst consensus, dated after the 10-K, rates the stock Buy with a target price of $525.51 (range $398.47 to $660.00) [3].
market_position:
Broadcom sells through a concentrated set of channels and customers. Distributors accounted for 48% of net revenue in both fiscal 2025 and fiscal 2024, and one distributor for 32%, up from 28% [1]. Management estimates that the top five end customers were about 40% of revenue in both years [1]. Those customers include hyperscalers, AI frontier-model companies, OEMs and, in software, large enterprises; the filing does not name individual end customers [1]. This concentration is the central feature of the market position, because a change in one large buyer's orders can move group revenue materially.

Geographically, revenue shipped to China, including Hong Kong, was 17% of fiscal 2025 revenue, down from 20% a year earlier, and the company states that its end-customer exposure to China is substantially smaller [1]. The filing does not disclose market share, so Broadcom's competitive position cannot be quantified from the 10-K alone [1]. Market data from the filing date show a closing price of $323.61, a market capitalisation of about $1.56 trillion, and a 52-week range of $136.52 to $411.55 [2]. The share price has therefore more than doubled from its 52-week low, and the share performance chart in this report shows the relative move against the S&P 500 [2].

Analyst consensus, dated after the 10-K, rates the stock Buy with a target price of $525.51, against a range of $398.47 to $660.00 [3]. Consensus expects FY2026 revenue of $105,981 million, growth of 65.9% [3]. That expectation depends on large AI customer deployments, which the filing says are timed unevenly and make quarterly revenue volatile [1]. The filing also notes that a shift toward hyperscale cloud may reduce volume in traditional enterprise data centres [1]. Market position is therefore strongest where AI infrastructure demand meets software licensing, and weakest where a single distributor or customer controls the timing of orders [1].
operating_results:
Revenue rose 24% to $63,887 million from $51,574 million. Fiscal 2024 had 53 weeks, so the comparison is not fully like-for-like [1]. Semiconductor revenue rose 22% and software revenue rose 26% [1]. Cost of revenue grew 8% to $20,593 million, while R&D rose 18% to $10,977 million, mainly on stock-based compensation of $7,568 million, up from $5,670 million [1]. Gross margin reached 68% against 63% a year earlier, and operating margin reached 40% against 26% [1].

Operating income rose to $25,484 million from $13,463 million [1]. Net margin reached 36% against 11%, but that figure was lifted by a $397 million tax benefit, compared with a $3,748 million tax provision in fiscal 2024 [1]. Diluted EPS was $4.77 against $1.23, yet pretax income rose sharply, so the operating line is the better guide to underlying growth [1]. Tax incentives reduced the fiscal 2025 provision by $2,709 million and added $0.56 to diluted EPS [1]. The global minimum tax is expected to have a material effect in fiscal 2026 [1].

Operating cash flow rose to $27,537 million from $19,962 million, but working capital absorbed $8,500 million, including a $2,717 million receivables build [1]. Free cash flow was $26,914 million [2]. Investing outflow fell to $580 million from $23,070 million, because the prior year included $25,416 million paid for VMware [1]. Financing outflow reached $20,127 million, including $11,142 million of dividends and $6,310 million of share repurchases and withholding taxes [1]. Cash ended at $16,178 million [1]. On a trailing basis to the latest quarter, free cash flow reached $39,403 million [2]. The results show strong cash generation, but the gap between operating income and reported net margin means the quality of earnings should be judged on operating cash flow.
risk_assessment:
The three risks that matter most in the filing are concentrated AI-driven demand, dependence on a single foundry, and gross margin pressure [1]. Customer concentration is the first. The top five end customers were about 40% of revenue, and some AI customers may need deferred or financed payment terms [1]. The filing warns that customer financing arrangements may increase exposure to credit and customer default risk [1]. Total indebtedness at November 2, 2025 was $67,120 million, so Broadcom could end up carrying customer credit risk on top of its own debt service [1]. The filing also states that AI-related growth may not be sustainable [1].

Supply concentration is the second. Approximately 95% of wafers made by contract manufacturers in fiscal 2025 were produced by TSMC, and about two-thirds of manufacturing materials came from five suppliers, some of them single source [1]. Manufacturing services are on a purchase-order basis with no minimum quantities and no long-term capacity commitments [1]. TSMC has raised wafer prices and could reprioritise capacity on short notice, and the filing notes that qualifying a new foundry is a lengthy and expensive process [1]. Two Broadcom facilities are themselves sole sources for specific product lines [1].

Margin and tax risk form the third group. The filing states that the sale or leasing of AI racks based on XPUs will likely increase operating margin but compress gross margin, which would weigh on the stock price [1]. The global minimum tax is expected to materially increase the effective tax rate and cash tax costs for fiscal 2026 [1]. The VMware spin-off from Dell carries a contingent tax exposure if the transaction is not tax-free, and the filing does not quantify it [1]. Valuation adds a further risk. EV/EBITDA rose from 11.67 in 2022 to 51.89 in 2025, so the share price already assumes continued earnings growth [2]. Taken together, these risks would hit revenue, credit exposure and margin at the same time in an AI spending slowdown [1][2].
competitors_analysis:
Three US-listed peers were chosen, business model first and size second. Marvell (MRVL, revenue about 0.1x Broadcom's) is the closest model, because it sells data-infrastructure semiconductors for data-centre and networking use [4]. NVIDIA (NVDA) is the main rival in AI accelerators and networking, although it is much larger [4]. AMD (AMD, about half Broadcom's revenue) competes directly in data-centre AI accelerators and is the closest in size [4]. Intel, Micron and Qualcomm were excluded because their core businesses are less comparable.

Broadcom's fiscal 2025 revenue growth of 23.9% trailed NVIDIA's 114.2% and AMD's 34.3%, but was well above Marvell's 4.7% [4]. Gross margin of 67.8% was below NVIDIA's 75.0%, but well above AMD's 49.5% and Marvell's 41.3% [4]. EBITDA margin of 54.3% sat between NVIDIA's 66.0% and AMD's 21.0% [4]. These comparisons show that Broadcom's profit profile is among the strongest in the group, while its growth rate is lower than NVIDIA's [4].

Returns are the weaker side of the picture. Broadcom's ROIC was 13.2% in 2025, after falling from 24.7% in 2023 to 6.4% in 2024 [4]. NVIDIA's ROIC was 83.3%, AMD's 4.8% and Marvell's negative 4.0% [4]. Broadcom's free cash flow conversion of 1.16 on the stated basis was above NVIDIA's 0.83 and below AMD's 1.55. The table did not define the conversion denominator, so this comparison should be read with caution [4]. Valuation is the other side of the comparison. Broadcom's EV/EBITDA of 51.89 sat above NVIDIA's 34.14 and AMD's 47.75, and below Marvell's 155.2, which reflects depressed earnings rather than a premium [2][4]. Broadcom moved from the cheapest multiple in the group in 2023 to above two of its three peers in 2025 [4]. The premium is justified only if EBITDA growth continues and ROIC recovers toward its 2023 level [4]. The peer comparison spans different fiscal calendars, so year-by-year readings are only approximate [4].

investment_theses.thesis: AI demand keeps semiconductor revenue growing fast enough to support consensus FY2026 revenue of about $106 billion.
investment_theses.evidence: Semiconductor revenue rose 22% to $36,858 million in fiscal 2025 on custom AI accelerators and AI networking [1]. Consensus expects FY2026 revenue of $105,981 million, growth of 65.9% [3].
investment_theses.signpost: Semiconductor revenue growth of at least 40% year on year in the fiscal 2026 10-K, due by early December 2026 (fiscal year ends November 1, 2026).
investment_theses.invalidation: Semiconductor revenue growth below 20% in any fiscal 2026 quarter, or a cut in FY2026 consensus revenue of more than 10%.

investment_theses.thesis: Infrastructure software keeps its high margin as the subscription transition continues.
investment_theses.evidence: Software operating income rose 49% to $20,765 million on $27,029 million of revenue, helped by lower labour costs after the VMware integration [1].
investment_theses.signpost: Software operating income growth of at least 25% in the fiscal 2026 10-K, due by early December 2026.
investment_theses.invalidation: Software operating income growth below 10% in fiscal 2026, which would show the 2025 gain was temporary.

investment_theses.thesis: Gross margin holds near 68% even as AI rack sales grow, so the margin expansion lasts.
investment_theses.evidence: Gross margin reached 68% against 63% in fiscal 2024 [1]. The filing says AI rack sales will likely compress gross margin [1].
investment_theses.signpost: Reported gross margin of at least 66% in each fiscal 2026 quarter, reviewed quarterly from the first quarter of fiscal 2026.
investment_theses.invalidation: Quarterly gross margin below 63%, the fiscal 2024 level, once AI rack shipments become material.

investment_theses.thesis: Earnings estimates keep rising, so the current valuation stays supported by consensus rather than requiring a higher growth rate.
investment_theses.evidence: FY2027 EPS consensus is $19.33, down 1.0% over 90 days, with 2 analysts raising and none cutting in the last 30 days [3]. The reverse DCF implies 26.6% annual revenue growth for ten years [2].
investment_theses.signpost: FY2027 EPS consensus holds at or above $19 through the fiscal 2026 10-K, due by early December 2026.
investment_theses.invalidation: FY2027 EPS consensus is cut by more than 10%, or the stock trades above 40x forward earnings without a matching earnings upgrade.
